intro_html: Employee Turnover & Absence Dashboard answers the questions an HR manager gets asked in every management meeting — how many people we have, who joined, who left, what our turnover is — on one screen in Employees, with every figure clickable, so the answer comes out of the employee records instead of a spreadsheet kept alongside them.

features.title: Five figures, one screen
features.desc: Headcount, joined, left, off today and turnover, side by side in the Employees app.

features.title: Every figure opens its list
features.desc: Press a number and the list that opens holds exactly that many rows; both come from the same query.

features.title: Joiners and leavers over time
features.desc: One line per arrival and per departure, groupable and chartable by month, department or reason.

features.title: Absence measured, not counted
features.desc: Ranks by the Bradford factor, so eleven separate single days outrank one three-week holiday.

features.title: The period is yours to set
features.desc: Defaults to the calendar year; the point-in-time figures ignore it and say so on the tile.

features.title: Approvals across the suite
features.desc: Everything in the wider OdoMate HR suite that is awaiting approval, in one list - free at github.com/OdoMate-Org/example-modules. Without those modules it stays empty.

features.title: Read-only, and provably so
features.desc: Creates no records, grants no group to anybody and never uses sudo(); figures honour each reader's own permissions.

features.title: Multi-company aware
features.desc: Record rules on both analysis models, so a reader sees their own companies and no others.

limitations: Read-only by design. There is no way to correct a wrong figure from this screen; fix the underlying employee version or time-off record instead.

Arrivals depend on a contract start date. Employees whose versions carry no contract start date never appear as joiners and never count towards headcount at a date, so if your data is thin here, turnover will read low.
Headcount at a date is reconstructed from movements, not from a historical snapshot, so retroactive edits to a contract start or departure date change past figures.
The Bradford figures have no time window. Filters select employees, not date ranges of leave - which differs from tools that recompute the factor per period.
Time off sitting in Second Approval is excluded on purpose. If your leave types use two-step approval, those absences are invisible here until the second approval lands.
Off today uses UTC day boundaries. In a database spread across far-apart time zones, an employee at the very edge of the day may be counted a few hours early or late.
